presentation.label: BUCKET BRIGADE
presentation.summary: A bucket-brigade delay: compander, clock-tracking filters, bucket noise, a resonant feedback tilt, freeze, a feedback governor and an input high-pass.
presentation.overview: The mono sum goes through a BBD chain: an optional input high-pass, a tanh into a 2:1 feedback compressor, an 8th-order anti-alias filter at a third of the clock, a bucket line clocked at 5.1 to 20.5 kHz with a charge-transfer polynomial and noise, a 9th-order reconstruction filter and the expander. FDBK returns the wet through a tilt with a sweepable bandpass; LIM governs how loud self-oscillation gets; FRZ holds the line. TIME glides the clock, so moving it bends the pitch of the line. The dry signal is never processed.
highlights: The clock sets the delay: longer repeats are darker and grainier, as on a BBD chip
TIME glides the clock over 20 ms: locks and LFOs bend the pitch of the repeats
1,023 or 4,095 buckets: 50 to 200 ms (the default) or 200 to 800 ms
TONE right of centre: a treble shelf; left: a resonant bandpass that FREQ places at 400 Hz-2 kHz
FRZ: from longer trails to an endless loop of the line, made for the crossfader
LIM keeps self-oscillation at a set level; HPF cuts bass into the line, 20 to 400 Hz
MIX 0 is the exact dry signal
usage: Choose BBD DELAY in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to the end of the list and press YES. The SETUP page holds STGS (bucket count) on encoder A, LIM on C and HPF on E.
On the main page: TIME (A), FDBK (B), FRZ (C), TONE (D), FREQ (E) and MIX (F).
With TONE towards either end the loop rings on from about FDBK 40; LIM (default 127, strongest) sets how loud it gets, and TIME or FREQ then sweep it.
The six main-page knobs take parameter locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC like any stock effect's; the SETUP knobs are set per Part.

controls.name: TIME
controls.doc: The bucket clock, 20.5 kHz at 0 to 5.1 kHz at 127, linear in delay time and gliding over 20 ms. The delay is 50-200 ms (STGS 1024) or 200-800 ms (4096). Not tempo-synced.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: The wet returned to the input through TONE. With TONE centred the repeats ring longer up to 127 (about 1 dB a second) but never self-oscillate; with TONE at either end the loop rings on from about FDBK 40, at a level LIM sets.

controls.name: FRZ
controls.doc: Freeze: rising from 0 the input fades out of the line and FDBK goes towards sustain for the current TONE (never down), so trails lengthen; at 127 the line loops its contents exactly at the level it had, ignoring input and FDBK. Crossfades of any speed into 127 keep the level. TIME changes the frozen loop's speed and pitch; a STGS change clears it.

controls.name: TONE
controls.doc: Bipolar, centre flat. The feedback tilt, 9 dB at the ends: right raises treble and cuts bass about 200 Hz; left adds a bandpass peak at FREQ, Q 1.5. Acts only inside the feedback loop.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: The centre of TONE's bandpass, 400 Hz to 2 kHz, logarithmic; 64 is about 900 Hz. Heard only with TONE left of centre; right of centre it does nothing.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: 0 is exactly dry. To 64 the wet rises to unity over the whole dry; from 64 to 127 the dry fades out, leaving the wet alone.

controls.name: STGS
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder A. Bucket count, so the delay range: 1024 (default) gives 50-200 ms, 4096 gives 200-800 ms. A change fades the wet out, clears the line (about 6 ms, dry) and fades back in. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: LIM
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder C. The feedback governor, 0 off, 127 (default) strongest: above a threshold of the wet's envelope FDBK is scaled by the square of the overshoot, so self-oscillation settles about 30 dB under LIM 0.

controls.name: HPF
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder E. 0 is off. Otherwise a 12 dB/octave Butterworth high-pass on the signal entering the bucket line, 20 Hz at 1 to 400 Hz at 127, logarithmic (64 is about 90 Hz); it glides like FREQ.

limitations: Hardware: on the owner's MKII over USB (15 October 2026): install, both cores, two instances on core 1, Part switches, removal and reinstall, the stop kill and its release, chip load. MKI, MIDI load, project save and reload and a power cycle on this version, and the card build's stop-kill hook on hardware are untested.

On today's beta base a DSP core holds BBD's 1,112 words beside what the bank's Parts keep loaded there: core 0 (T5-T8) has 2,361 words, so a bank whose Parts keep DARK REV on T5-T8 refuses BBD there (DSP MEMORY FULL); core 1 (T1-T4) has 3,234. One instance a core fits the DSP budget beside seven stock effects; a second fits on core 1 only.
Over USB it needs the Modwerk beta base with the ev_tail_kill event (ba89721d or later) and keeps its card effect id, 14: a set where another module holds id 14 is refused.
FX2 only: the bucket line needs the 16K-word delay buffer the OS gives FX2 instances.

With stock DSP code built in, BBD's 1,112 words take the space of SPRING REV and PLATE REV, which leave the FX2 chooser (DARK REV calls a 35-word routine inside SPRING REV's code, so BBD is placed from PLATE REV's start, clear of it); a saved project that uses either on FX2 plays that slot dry. Every other stock effect stays, DARK REV bit-identical to stock. Other modules in the same build can change the choice.
Free-running TIME: the DSP side has no tempo word, so the delay does not follow tempo, track speed or swing.
Mono bucket line: the wet is the same on both channels; the dry stays stereo.
Aliasing is the bucket brigade's own: -44 dBc for a 1.1 kHz tone at the fastest clock, -37 dBc at the slowest.

Dearer than any stock effect: up to 400 executed instructions per sample with trig splits (SPRING REV 314, CHORUS 293, DJ EQ 331), 363 without splits. Four per core fit the static budget; real-chip headroom is not measured.
STGS, LIM and HPF are on the SETUP page: the OS does not lock, modulate or scene them.

storage.label: DSP program / buffer
storage.conditions: 1,112 assembled program words on each DSP core in the space of SPRING REV and PLATE REV; a 91-word X state block per instance (r7+$00..$5a); up to 4,095 ring words plus 58 coefficient words of the 16,384 Y words the OS allocates to every FX2 instance.

processing.label: DSP instruction peak
processing.conditions: benchmark_stock_dsp.py's method (one instance per core, 16-sample blocks, null stub subtracted) with SPRING REV, CHORUS and DJ EQ through the same cases: worst case 399.31 with a trig split, 363.06 unsplit. Static loop count 378 cycles/sample. Executed instructions, not chip cycles.

impact.conditions: One active instance at its dearest settings with moving controls and trig splits; the 16K buffer is the stock FX2 allocation, reused.

cpu.rationale: A few ColdFire instructions run only while STOP, STOP, STOP holds a track (a hook on card builds, the base's ev_tail_kill over USB); the stock parameter pages publish the knobs, as for any FX2 effect.

dsp.rationale: 399.31 executed instructions/sample worst case with trig splits against SPRING REV 314.19, CHORUS 293.06 and DJ EQ 330.94 (the dearest stock effect) under the same cases; four per core are 1,512 of 3,120 static cycles. Chip timing is unmeasured.

memory.rationale: 1,112 program words per core in the space of SPRING REV and PLATE REV, a 91-word X block per instance, the 16K-word FX2 delay buffer every delay already gets.

tests.summary: Render gates pass on a native image (52): exact dry at MIX 0, the DSP against its float reference across every control including HPF, trig splits, STGS changes with TIME still and moving, the stop-kill input, freeze, idle tails and the LIM level, eight-instance isolation under guard and dirty start, garbage start and no zipper. Matched benchmark: 399.31 executed instructions/sample with trig splits (0.1.0: 439.44), 363.06 unsplit; output bit-identical to 0.1.0 in all 45 benchmark cases. On the owner's MKII over USB: installed, picked on T1, T2 and T5, Part switches, removal and reinstall, self-test, the stop kill cutting the tail to -132 dBFS and its release; 453-527 chip cycles a sample measured.
gates: verify.py: init rules, static cycles, native placement, exact dry, reference match (HPF at 1, 64, 127), splits, stages (TIME still and moving), the stop-kill input, freeze, idle and LIM level, eight-instance isolation (-guard -dirty), garbage start, zipper census
evidence/performance.json: perf.py bench (stock benchmark under matched cases) and a 32 s eight-instance stress render
npm run module:verify: browser builder against native octabam

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to BBD DELAY at the end of the effect list and press YES. Turn encoder A (STGS) to 4096.

Press FX2 for the main page. Turn encoder F (MIX) to 48 and encoder B (FDBK) to 70, play a sample and turn encoder A (TIME): repeats between 200 and 800 ms, darker the longer they get. Turn encoder D (TONE) left and sweep encoder E (FREQ) for resonant repeats; turn encoder C (FRZ) to 127 to loop the line.
Turn FDBK back to 0 and MIX to 0 to hear the exact dry signal, or set FX2 back to DELAY or NONE in FX2 SETUP to remove the effect.

conditions.parameterExtremes: cycle_count.py prices the per-sample loop with the bucket tick taken and HPF on (378); the per-call bound charges every word outside the loop once, the clear and run paths together, all fixed-loop iterations, the nine-section rotation of a reset (in the clear call before it since 0.1.1), HPF's section and every helper call, so every knob endpoint is covered.
conditions.parameterModulation: Two calls per 16-frame block cover trigger splits, each charged the full per-call bound. LFOs, locks, scenes and CC reach the same knob words. No contention or silicon wall-clock timing is claimed.
conditions.modeSwitching: STGS changes (fade, clear, reset), FRZ 127, HPF on and off and the hidden stop-kill input (dry and clear) are inside the union bound.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight FX2 instances, four per DSP core, at 44.1 kHz and 16 frames per block: 44,992 per core within the SDK 49,920 module allowance; the stock/scheduling reserve stays separate. Arbitrary companion load and real-chip contention are unmeasured. On the owner's MKII one instance measured 453-527 chip cycles a sample (evidence/usb-hardware.md).
conditions.inputConditions: The word-span bound does not depend on sample values; the tick path, saturation, feedback, silence, impulses and full-scale inputs are covered. Render gates and the matched benchmark (at most 399.31 executed instructions/sample) are in TESTING.md.

regions.name: Used and initialized stock X state, r7+0..0x5a
Reserved remainder of 256-word stock X block
Reserved stock FX2 Y buffer: ring up to 4,095 words, 58 coefficient words
System stack, six entries of two words on both cores
Stop-kill ColdFire code (card hook 32 bytes; USB handler 22 bytes)

memory.conditions: The stock 256-word X block and 16,384-word Y buffer per FX2 instance, including unused padding; code shared once per core. No authored heap or SDRAM arena; the stop kill's ColdFire code is a straight-line hook or event handler with no stack of its own. The system stack is bounded by the rotation's do, a bsr and its divide's do on each core. Logical 24-bit DSP words; flash descriptors use byte accounting. Guarded eight-instance software evidence does not claim hardware canaries.

hardware.tester: repeat98's unit, driven over USB by Claude Code
hardware.summary: The USB package (614bf23b...) on a RAM-booted development twin of the beta base with ev_tail_kill (e429b787..., MAIN bf2ab8a5...), on the owner's MKII: installed (stage, trial, keep); picked on T1 and T2 (core 1) and T5 (core 0); a second instance on core 0 refused by the DSP budget as designed; a Part switch away and back keeps every knob; removal refused while in use, taken when not, the Part then plays dry with BBD listed missing, and a reinstall restores it; the base's self-test passed; STOP, STOP, STOP zeroed BBD's slot 11 in the track's frame record and cut a ringing tail to -132 dBFS, released by the track's next trig; one instance cost 453-469 chip cycles a sample at the defaults and 527 at the dearest settings.
limitations: Driven by an agent with the owner's permission; the owner was not asked to listen. Audio was checked from USB recordings.
No project save and reload or power cycle on this version (RAM-booted base, owner's project not saved); MKI, MIDI load and the card build's stop-kill hook on hardware are untested.
Chip cycles come from the base's idle counters at steady settings with the transport stopped; a trig split's worst block was not measured on the chip.
